product.name: Bacteriostatic Water — Laboratory Preparation Solution (RUO)
product.description:
Bacteriostatic Water is a sterile aqueous solution containing a preservative component studied for its role in inhibiting microbial growth during laboratory preparation and compound handling processes.

Supplied for analytical research, solution stability testing, and non-clinical investigational applications. Not intended for medical or veterinary administration.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal use.
product.compoundClass: Preserved aqueous diluent — Water for Injection containing benzyl alcohol as a bacteriostatic preservative
product.otherNames: Bacteriostatic Water for Injection, USP; BWFI; bacteriostatic WFI; preserved water for injection; water (CAS 7732-18-5) preserved with benzyl alcohol (CAS 100-51-6)
product.molecularFormula: H2O (with benzyl alcohol C7H8O as preservative)
product.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
product.technicalOverview:
Bacteriostatic Water for Injection, USP is a sterile, non-pyrogenic preparation of Water for Injection to which benzyl alcohol has been added as a bacteriostatic preservative. The standard US presentation contains 0.9% (9 mg/mL) benzyl alcohol; some labelled products use 1.1% (11 mg/mL). It contains no added buffer and no antimicrobial agent other than the benzyl alcohol.

The preservative is what defines the product. Benzyl alcohol (phenylmethanol, C7H8O, 108.14 g/mol, CAS 100-51-6) is bacteriostatic rather than bactericidal — it inhibits the growth of organisms introduced during handling but does not sterilise a contaminated solution. This is precisely what permits the multiple-dose format: repeated withdrawals may be made from the same vial to dissolve or dilute compounds, whereas preservative-free Sterile Water for Injection must be entered only once. Preservative effectiveness is finite; conventional in-use practice is to discard a broached multiple-dose vial within 28 days.

SAFETY — NEONATAL CONTRAINDICATION. Benzyl alcohol is toxic to neonates and is the agent implicated in gasping syndrome, a fatal toxic syndrome described in low-birth-weight infants exposed to benzyl-alcohol-preserved flush solutions and diluents. FDA labelling for this product carries the warning NOT FOR USE IN NEONATES. Where water is required to prepare or dilute a preparation for a newborn, only preservative-free Sterile Water for Injection is appropriate.

Benzyl alcohol is not chemically inert. It is a documented cause of protein aggregation and can accelerate degradation of peptide and protein solutes, so it is not a suitable diluent where the solute's stability in the presence of an aromatic alcohol has not been established. Confirm solute compatibility before selecting bacteriostatic rather than preservative-free water.
product.storageHandling: Supplied as multiple-dose vials in 3 mL, 5 mL, 10 mL, 20 mL and 30 mL sizes. Store at 20-25 °C (68-77 °F); excursions permitted to 15-30 °C. Do not freeze. Swab the stopper with 70% isopropyl alcohol before each entry. Because the vial is preserved, repeated withdrawals are permitted — record the date of first entry and discard within 28 days of broaching, or sooner if the label directs. Discard immediately if the solution is not clear and colourless, if particulate matter is visible, or if the vial seal has been compromised. Not for use in neonates. Do not use as a diluent for compounds shown to be incompatible with benzyl alcohol.
product.citations: Gershanik J, Boecler B, Ensley H, McCloskey S, George W. The Gasping Syndrome and Benzyl Alcohol Poisoning. New England Journal of Medicine. 1982;307(22):1384-1388. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM198211253072206

related.name: 5Amino 1mq
related.description:
5-Amino-1MQ is a small-molecule NNMT pathway inhibitor studied for its role in cellular energy regulation and metabolic signaling research models. It is frequently utilized in investigations involving adipocyte metabolism and NAD+-related pathways.

This material is supplied in research format exclusively for analytical testing and non-clinical investigational applications.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.compoundClass: Small-molecule quaternary quinolinium cation; selective, membrane-permeable inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT)
related.otherNames:
5-Amino-1-methylquinolinium chloride
5-Amino-1MQ
5-amino-1-methylquinolinium
Note: registry 42464-96-0 is used by most suppliers for the chloride, but is also cited for the iodide salt; identifiers here describe the CHLORIDE.
related.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
5-Amino-1MQ is a small, permanently charged quinolinium cation carrying an amino substituent at the 5-position and a methyl group on the ring nitrogen. Despite the fixed positive charge it is reported to be membrane-permeable, which is the property that distinguishes it from earlier bisubstrate NNMT inhibitors and makes cell-based and whole-animal work practical.

Its described target is nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), a cytosolic enzyme that transfers a methyl group from S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) to nicotinamide, producing 1-methylnicotinamide and S-adenosylhomocysteine. Because nicotinamide is a salvage-pathway precursor of NAD+, NNMT activity sits at a junction between methyl-group economy and NAD+ availability; inhibiting the enzyme is the mechanistic rationale behind investigating this compound in adipocyte metabolism and NAD+-related pathway models.

Identity note: this material is most often supplied as a salt rather than the free cation, and the salt form is not stated on the product record. Published and vendor sources disagree on which registry number belongs to which salt — one widely circulated page pairs a chloride name with an iodide molecular formula — so no CAS number is asserted here. Confirm the counter-ion, salt stoichiometry and assigned registry number against the lot-specific certificate of analysis before using this material in any quantitative work, since salt form changes the molar mass and therefore every concentration calculated by weight.

The evidence base is preclinical. Reported effects come from cell culture and rodent studies; no human clinical trial data are cited here.
related.researchApplications: Used in vitro and in rodent models as a chemical probe of NNMT function. Reported preclinical applications include: interrogation of adipocyte lipid handling and energy expenditure in diet-induced obesity models; study of the SAM/methylation and NAD+ salvage axis and how NNMT inhibition redistributes flux between them; and investigation of muscle stem cell proliferation, fusion and regenerative capacity in aged skeletal muscle. Appropriate experimental controls include an NNMT-null or knockdown comparator and direct measurement of 1-methylnicotinamide, since a fall in that metabolite is the most direct readout of on-target engagement.
related.storageHandling: Supplied as 5 mg of solid material. Store the dry solid desiccated at -20 °C, protected from light and moisture; the compound is reported to be soluble in DMSO and in aqueous buffer. Prepare concentrated stocks in anhydrous DMSO, aliquot to avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles, and store aliquots at -20 °C or below. Allow vials to equilibrate to room temperature before opening to prevent condensation onto hygroscopic solid. Weigh in a fume hood and handle with gloves and eye protection. Calculate molarity from the salt form stated on the certificate of analysis, not from the free-cation mass.
related.citations:
Neelakantan H, Vance V, Wetzel MD, et al. Selective and membrane-permeable small molecule inhibitors of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase reverse high fat diet-induced obesity in mice. Biochemical Pharmacology. 2018;147:141-152. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bcp.2017.11.007
Neelakantan H, Brightwell CR, Graber TG, et al. Small molecule nicotinamide N-methyltransferase inhibitor activates senescent muscle stem cells and improves regenerative capacity of aged skeletal muscle. Biochemical Pharmacology. 2019;163:481-492. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bcp.2019.02.008

related.name: L-Glutathione (Lyophilized) — Redox Signaling Reference Compound (RUO)
related.description:
L-Glutathione is a naturally occurring tripeptide composed of glutamine, cysteine, and glycine studied in laboratory research for its role in cellular redox balance and oxidative signaling pathways. Research investigations commonly examine glutathione-dependent enzymatic systems, intracellular antioxidant regulatory mechanisms, and thiol-mediated biochemical interactions in non-clinical environments.

This material is supplied in lyophilized research format for analytical testing, stability assessment, and non-clinical investigational applications. Lyophilized format is provided solely to support controlled laboratory handling and does not indicate suitability for clinical or veterinary administration.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.compoundClass: Endogenous thiol tripeptide; principal intracellular antioxidant and redox buffer, supplied lyophilised
related.otherNames: GSH; reduced glutathione; L-glutathione reduced; gamma-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinylglycine; gamma-Glu-Cys-Gly; isothion; glutathione (reduced form)
related.sequence: gamma-Glu-Cys-Gly (γ-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinylglycine; three residues, N-terminal glutamate joined through its gamma-carboxyl rather than the alpha-carboxyl)
related.technicalOverview:
L-Glutathione is a tripeptide of glutamate, cysteine and glycine and the most abundant low-molecular-weight thiol in the cell, present intracellularly at millimolar concentration. Its defining structural feature is the gamma-peptide bond: the N-terminal glutamate is linked through its side-chain gamma-carboxyl group rather than the usual alpha-carboxyl. That single unconventional linkage is functionally decisive — it makes the molecule resistant to ordinary intracellular peptidases, so glutathione is not degraded by the general proteolytic machinery and can be maintained at high steady-state concentration.

Glutathione is synthesised in two ATP-dependent steps, by glutamate-cysteine ligase (the rate-limiting step, feedback-inhibited by GSH itself) and then glutathione synthetase. Its chemistry is carried by the cysteine sulfhydryl. Two molecules of GSH oxidise to the disulfide GSSG, and the GSH/GSSG couple constitutes the cell's principal redox buffer; the ratio is a standard experimental readout of oxidative status. GSH is the reducing substrate for glutathione peroxidases, which detoxify hydrogen peroxide and lipid hydroperoxides, and the nucleophilic conjugating partner for glutathione S-transferases, which is the first step of the mercapturic acid pathway for electrophile and xenobiotic disposal. Glutathione reductase regenerates GSH from GSSG at the expense of NADPH, coupling redox defence to the pentose phosphate pathway.

The material is supplied lyophilised because glutathione in aqueous solution oxidises to GSSG on exposure to air, at neutral to alkaline pH, and in the presence of trace transition metals. A solution left standing is progressively a different molecule from the one that was weighed out. The dry powder is comparatively stable; the reconstituted solution is not.

Evidence for systemic administration is largely preclinical and mechanistic. Oral glutathione is extensively hydrolysed presystemically, which is the usual argument advanced for parenteral routes, but controlled human outcome data remain limited.
related.researchApplications: Used as a redox-active reference compound and as a reagent. Common applications include: maintaining reducing conditions in buffers for enzyme assays and protein handling, and as the reducing agent in redox-shuffle buffers for in vitro protein refolding; serving as the substrate for glutathione peroxidase, glutathione reductase and glutathione S-transferase activity assays; establishing GSH/GSSG ratio standards for quantifying cellular oxidative status; and as the elution agent for GST-tagged fusion protein purification on glutathione affinity resins. In cell and animal models it is used to probe thiol-dependent detoxification, electrophile conjugation and oxidative-stress signalling. Because it oxidises readily, prepare solutions fresh and include an internal check of the GSH/GSSG ratio in quantitative work.
related.storageHandling: Supplied lyophilised as 1500 mg or 600 mg per vial, in boxes of 10 vials. Store the sealed lyophilised powder at 2-8 °C (refrigerated), desiccated and protected from light; the dry form is far more stable than any solution. Allow vials to reach room temperature before opening so that moisture does not condense onto the hygroscopic cake. Reconstitute with a preservative-free diluent, directing the stream against the vial wall and swirling rather than shaking — vigorous agitation aerates the solution and accelerates oxidation to GSSG. Use reconstituted solution promptly; do not store it at room temperature or hold it overnight in an aerated container. Protect solutions from light and avoid contact with trace metals, oxidising agents and alkaline pH. Discard if the cake is discoloured, if it fails to dissolve cleanly, or if a reconstituted solution develops turbidity or a sulfurous odour.
related.citations:
Forman HJ, Zhang H, Rinna A. Glutathione: Overview of its protective roles, measurement, and biosynthesis. Molecular Aspects of Medicine. 2009;30(1-2):1-12. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mam.2008.08.006
Lu SC. Glutathione synthesis. Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - General Subjects. 2013;1830(5):3143-3153. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbagen.2012.09.008

related.name: Methylcobalamin (Methylated Vitamin B12)
related.description:
Methylcobalamin is a methylated form of vitamin B12 studied in laboratory research for its role as a cofactor in methylation-dependent enzymatic pathways and cellular metabolic processes. Research investigations commonly examine its involvement in methionine synthase activity, intracellular methyl group transfer reactions, and biochemical signaling associated with cellular metabolism in non-clinical environments.

This material is supplied in sterile solution format for analytical testing, stability evaluation, and non-clinical investigational research applications. Format is provided solely to support controlled laboratory handling and does not indicate suitability for clinical or veterinary administration.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.compoundClass: Cobalamin (vitamin B12) coenzyme form; organometallic cobalt corrinoid and enzymatic methyl-group donor
related.otherNames: Mecobalamin; MeCbl; MeB12; methylated vitamin B12; methylcobalamin; cobalamin, methyl-; coenzyme B12 (methyl form)
related.sequence: Not applicable — small-molecule compound, not a peptide (no amino acid sequence)
related.technicalOverview:
Methylcobalamin is one of the two coenzyme forms of vitamin B12 found in human metabolism. It is a corrinoid: a cobalt ion held at the centre of a corrin macrocycle, with a 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole nucleotide coordinating from the lower (alpha) face and, in this form, a methyl group bonded directly to cobalt on the upper (beta) face. That cobalt-carbon bond makes methylcobalamin one of the very few naturally occurring organometallic compounds — a genuine metal-alkyl bond in a biological molecule.

It differs from cyanocobalamin, the synthetic form used in most supplements and in the standard US injectable, only in that upper axial ligand: cyanocobalamin carries a cyano group where methylcobalamin carries a methyl group. Cyanocobalamin is not itself a coenzyme and must be enzymatically dealkylated and reprocessed before use, whereas methylcobalamin is directly the cofactor for one of the two B12-dependent human enzymes.

That enzyme is methionine synthase (MTR), which remethylates homocysteine to methionine. The methyl group is taken from 5-methyltetrahydrofolate and passed to cobalt, forming methylcobalamin, and then transferred onward to homocysteine — the cobalt centre cycling between Co(I) and Co(III) as the methyl carrier. Methionine produced this way is the precursor of S-adenosylmethionine, the universal methyl donor for DNA, RNA, protein and phospholipid methylation. This reaction is also the point at which folate and B12 metabolism intersect, which is why B12 deficiency traps folate as 5-methyltetrahydrofolate and produces the megaloblastic changes characteristic of both deficiencies. The second human B12 enzyme, methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, uses adenosylcobalamin rather than methylcobalamin.

Methylcobalamin is intensely photolabile. Light cleaves the cobalt-carbon bond, converting it to hydroxocobalamin; this is not a slow degradation but a rapid photochemical reaction, and it is the single most important handling constraint on the molecule.
related.researchApplications: Used as the cofactor and reference standard in studies of methionine synthase activity and one-carbon metabolism, in assays of the folate/B12 methyl-transfer cycle, and as an analytical standard for cobalamin speciation by HPLC and LC-MS where distinguishing methyl-, adenosyl-, hydroxo- and cyanocobalamin matters. Also used as a model substrate in photochemistry of cobalt-carbon bonds. Note that unlike cyanocobalamin, methylcobalamin injection is not an FDA-approved product in the United States; comparative human data on the two forms are limited.
related.storageHandling: Supplied as 1000 mcg/mL sterile solution in 10 mL and 20 mL multiple-dose vials. PROTECT FROM LIGHT AT ALL TIMES — this is the critical requirement for this molecule, not a generic precaution: ambient light cleaves the cobalt-carbon bond within minutes and converts methylcobalamin to hydroxocobalamin. Keep vials in amber glass or in the original carton, work under subdued or filtered light, and do not leave a drawn syringe standing on the bench. Store refrigerated at 2-8 °C; do not freeze. The solution is deep red — fading toward pink or a shift in hue indicates photodegradation and the vial should be discarded. Swab the stopper before each entry, record the date of first entry and observe the labelled in-use period for the multiple-dose vial. Discard if particulate matter or turbidity appears.
related.citations: Green R, Allen LH, Bjørke-Monsen A-L, et al. Vitamin B12 deficiency. Nature Reviews Disease Primers. 2017;3:17040. https://doi.org/10.1038/nrdp.2017.40

related.name: Powered — Micronutrient Cofactor Research Blend (RUO)
related.description:
Powered is a multi-compound liquid formulation composed of vitamin-derived molecules studied in laboratory research for their roles as enzymatic cofactors and regulators of intracellular metabolic signaling pathways.

Niacinamide and niacin are investigated for their participation in nicotinamide-dependent metabolic reactions and coenzyme-associated biochemical processes. Thiamine hydrochloride is studied for its role in thiamine-dependent enzymatic systems involved in carbohydrate metabolism pathways. Pantothenic acid is examined as a precursor to coenzyme A within intracellular metabolic reactions. Choline and inositol are investigated for their involvement in cellular membrane signaling and phospholipid-associated biochemical pathways. Biotin is studied for its participation in carboxylase enzyme systems, while riboflavin functions as a precursor to flavin cofactors involved in oxidation-reduction reactions.

This material is supplied in liquid research format for analytical testing, stability assessment, and non-clinical investigational research applications. Liquid format is provided solely to support controlled laboratory handling and does not indicate suitability for clinical or veterinary administration.

For Research Use Only. Not for human or animal consumption.
related.compoundClass: Multi-component liquid formulation — B-vitamin and lipotropic micronutrient blend; no single active substance
related.otherNames: Components stated on the product record: niacinamide (nicotinamide), niacin (nicotinic acid), thiamine hydrochloride (vitamin B1), pantothenic acid (vitamin B5), choline, inositol
related.technicalOverview:
Powered is a multi-compound liquid formulation rather than a single chemical entity, so it has no molecular formula, molecular weight, IUPAC name or CAS registry number of its own. Those fields are left empty deliberately; the identity of the product is its component list, and each component has its own identifiers.

The components named on the product record are as follows.

Niacinamide (nicotinamide) and niacin (nicotinic acid) are the two vitamin B3 forms. Both are precursors of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) and its phosphate NADP+, the pyridine dinucleotide coenzymes that carry hydride in catabolic and anabolic redox reactions respectively. Niacinamide enters the NAD+ pool through the salvage pathway via NAMPT; niacin enters through the Preiss-Handler pathway. The two are not interchangeable in every respect — niacin is additionally an agonist at the GPR109A receptor, which niacinamide is not.

Thiamine hydrochloride (vitamin B1) is the precursor of thiamine pyrophosphate, the cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase and transketolase. Its thiazolium ring carbon is the catalytic centre for the decarboxylation chemistry these enzymes perform, placing thiamine at the entry point of carbohydrate carbon into the tricarboxylic acid cycle and at the non-oxidative branch of the pentose phosphate pathway.

Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is the precursor of coenzyme A and of the phosphopantetheine prosthetic group of acyl carrier protein. Coenzyme A carries acyl groups as thioesters throughout fatty acid oxidation and synthesis and into the TCA cycle as acetyl-CoA.

Choline is a quaternary ammonium precursor of phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin, the principal structural phospholipids of cell membranes, and of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine. It is also a methyl donor via betaine, linking it to the homocysteine remethylation cycle.

Inositol, as myo-inositol, is the head group of the phosphatidylinositol phospholipids, from which the second messengers inositol trisphosphate and diacylglycerol are generated on phospholipase C activation.

COMPOSITION NOTE: the product description available for this record is truncated and the full quantitative formula — concentrations per mL, salt forms of each component, vehicle and preservative — is not stated. The component list above reflects only what is explicitly named. The visible portion of this description is identical to that of the companion product Radiant, so the two cannot be distinguished from the record alone. Confirm the complete formula against the manufacturer's certificate of analysis before any calculation.
related.researchApplications: Supplied for research use only. As a multi-component blend rather than a defined single substance, it is unsuitable as an analytical reference standard; work requiring a known molar concentration of any individual vitamin should use that component as an individually characterised material with its own certificate of analysis.
related.storageHandling: Supplied as a blend in a 10 mL vial — a multiple-dose format. Store refrigerated at 2-8 °C unless the manufacturer's label directs otherwise; do not freeze. Protect from light: several components, thiamine in particular, are light-sensitive, and B-vitamin blends commonly discolour on exposure. Swab the stopper with 70% isopropyl alcohol before each entry, record the date of first entry and observe the labelled in-use period; confirm from the label whether the formulation is preserved, since an unpreserved blend must be treated as single-entry. B-vitamin solutions are characteristically yellow; discard if the colour darkens appreciably, or if turbidity or particulate matter appears. Thiamine is unstable at alkaline pH — avoid admixture with alkaline solutions.
